His entries are under his sign-in; signed out the page shows the example. Identify all saving functions and make sure push is made automatically as well as every 12 hours"; his answer: "Account-ID key (fastest)". The saving functions: the record (each transaction · Put back my entries) and the budget (every edit · Reset). Signed in, both are read back from the account once and merged without ever dropping an entry (a diverged copy is kept whole under its own name); every change after that is pushed (a short pause so a burst of typing is one write), and again every 12 hours while the page is open and on return when 12 hours have passed. Stored through the existing account table's guarded functions (no public table access), keyed by a SHA-256 of his sign-in id — the account-ID key he chose: anyone who learned his sign-in id could read it (recorded, his decision). A small cloud beside Transaction Record turns green when the account copy is written (its time on hold); crossed until then. Under the budget, his line (addendum 119, "Short"): "Plan the month. Watch spending by the minute. Keep your savings on track." No budget figure changes. |

The chart now opens on $/min: income, spending and net per minute from his own record (each deposit and withdrawal running over its own length, monthly ones repeating every 30 days across a longer span), drawn on the shared R-CORE chart engine (components/2525-core/rcore-chart.tsx, reusable by every 2525 app) with the numbers in the upper right following the finger, including the net by the span's end. A unit dropdown offers $/min · /sec · /hr · /day and $; $ keeps the balance view exactly as before. And (addendum 127 "remove this line") the legend line "- - Net • Upside / Savings +… · date" under the chart is gone. No budget figure changes. |
